limitations: Retrospective research designed today, not a prospectively untouched historical test.
Current-listed membership omits historical delisted firms and introduces survivorship bias.
Provider-adjusted prices are today's vintage. Signals may reflect later corrections.
Historical availability is imputed at exchange close plus one minute, not verified provider publication time.
Historical capture reconstructs nominal prices using provider-reported splits; missing or revised actions can still distort historical share affordability.
Daily marks anchor raw entry notional to adjusted-close ratios: synthetic total-return units, not a corporate-action cash ledger.
Training uses only the preceding 756 sessions; a selected rule is frozen for the next 252 sessions. All attempts and training scores are reported.
Selection uses the declared initial budget at 100 bps costs; test accounts compound their own wealth. Cash is selected when no candidate qualifies.
Next-close entries, nonoverlapping batches, no margin, whole shares, maximum five stocks, conservative T+3 sale settlement in every era.
Portfolios are in cash at each predetermined fold boundary; entries that cannot finish their full horizon before that boundary are skipped.
Any missing selected entry or held daily adjusted price invalidates that portfolio result; losses are never dropped from an average.
Costs are symmetric proportional fees and slippage per executed notional; taxes, fixed commissions, FX, borrow, interest and monthly contributions are excluded.
Full-period fixed-rule comparisons are descriptive; selecting their best result would reuse test data.
Drawdown is a positive loss fraction from the preceding daily equity peak; all returns are native currency with no FX conversion.
